SHOT: Straight-on e-commerce packshot, 4:5. ONE ring only, standing upright on the top face, the three stone bands stacked tightly together side by side as one broad ring, the plain gold band threaded through them and standing upright across the top of the stack, as in IMAGE 1, on a cream plaster cube. Camera close, a little above the cube's top face, looking down at about thirty degrees. Macro-sharp on the metal.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is the supplier's own product photograph of this exact piece and the ONLY authority on its design: copy its construction, its metal colour and its stone colour EXACTLY; it is the supplier's product sheet on white with printed labels and dashed lines: ignore every letter, number and line. IMAGE 2 shows the same ring worn by a model: use it only to see how the bands sit together on the finger. IMAGE 3 is here ONLY for the plinth, the camera distance, the background and the light: copy its cube and its framing exactly and ignore everything else about it.

CONSTRUCTION LOCK: AN INTERLOCKED STACK RING: three stone-set bands stacked tightly side by side as one broad ring, with a FOURTH slim plain band threaded through them: (1) a slim gold tone band about 3mm wide with a channel of small square-cut EMERALD-GREEN stones set edge to edge, between two gold rails; (2) a SILVER tone band about 3mm wide with a channel of small rectangular BAGUETTE-cut EMERALD-GREEN stones set end to end, between two bright silver rails; (3) the WIDEST band, a broad flat polished gold tone band about 5mm wide, clearly about twice as wide as each of the others, with about six small round EMERALD-GREEN stones sunk FLUSH into its flat surface, spaced apart, with no raised settings and no claws; (4) a slim plain polished gold tone band about 2mm wide looped through the stack, standing upright across its top like a ring threaded through a ring, as IMAGE 1 shows. Stacked, the three stone bands make one ring about 11mm wide. The silver band ALWAYS carries its green baguette channel, never plain silver; the gold channel band carries small squares and the wide band spaced rounds; a deep blue-green emerald, never grass green, never teal, never black; no white dots or accent stones between the channel stones; never a single band.

SCALE TEST: The three stone bands together are about 11mm wide (supplier's sheet); the green squares about 2mm; the baguettes about 1.5x3mm; the round green stones about 3mm. The piece keeps its true small size against the cube, never enlarged.

GROUND: The cream plaster cube fills the lower half of the frame, large and close; flat faces, softly rounded corners, fine plaster grain. Warm cream seamless behind with a gentle gradient falloff, never sand, tan, beige or golden. Soft large key from camera-left, one soft shadow, plus ONE small hard specular kicker from the right, so the metal shows a bright moving highlight and a dark rolled edge on every curve, and every stone shows internal sparkle and a hard white point, never flat colour.

ABSENCE LIST: No hand, no fingers, no model, no fabric, no props, no flowers, no box. No second piece of jewellery. Metal: polished gold tone and bright silver tone exactly where IMAGE 1 shows them. No lettering, no watermark, no logo, no tag, no size sticker anywhere in frame. No border, no frame, no paper edge, no vignette: the image fills the whole frame edge to edge. A clean modern digital photograph: no creases, no fold lines, no aged-paper texture, no scratches, no film grain.

SHOT: Straight-on e-commerce packshot, 4:5. ONE pair of earrings only, both studs lying flat side by side on the top face, the octagon tables facing up; each stone's outline is a REGULAR octagon like a stop sign, its eight sides equal, so it reads almost round, on a cream plaster cube. Camera close, a little above the cube's top face, looking down at about thirty degrees. Macro-sharp on the metal.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is a phone photograph of the actual piece and the ONLY authority on what it is: copy its construction, its metal colour and its stone colour EXACTLY; it is the owner's photo of one stud on a white display ear held between finger and thumb: take ONLY the stud; ignore the display ear and the hand. IMAGE 2 is a closer crop of the same stud. IMAGE 2 is a close detail of the same piece. IMAGE 3 is here ONLY for the plinth, the camera distance, the background and the light: copy its cube and its framing exactly and ignore everything else about it.

CONSTRUCTION LOCK: A PAIR OF OCTAGON SOLITAIRE STUDS: each stud is ONE OCTAGON-cut faceted stone, a REGULAR octagon with eight EQUAL straight sides (the four diagonal sides as long as the four straight ones), so it reads almost round, in a soft BLUSH PINK with peachy flashes, held in a slim gold setting with fine claws at its corners, on a single post. Exactly one stone per stud; a regular octagon with eight equal sides, never a square with small clipped corners, never Asscher, never round, never a hexagon; soft blush pink, never hot pink, never red, never lilac; no halo, no pave.

SCALE TEST: Each stone is about 9.5mm across, about half an earlobe. The piece keeps its true small size against the cube, never enlarged.

GROUND: The cream plaster cube fills the lower half of the frame, large and close; flat faces, softly rounded corners, fine plaster grain. Warm cream seamless behind with a gentle gradient falloff, never sand, tan, beige or golden. Soft large key from camera-left, one soft shadow, plus ONE small hard specular kicker from the right, so the metal shows a bright moving highlight and a dark rolled edge on every curve, and every stone shows internal sparkle and a hard white point, never flat colour.

ABSENCE LIST: No hand, no fingers, no model, no fabric, no props, no flowers, no box. No second piece of jewellery. Metal: warm 18k gold tone, never brassy, orange or greenish. No lettering, no watermark, no logo, no tag, no size sticker anywhere in frame. No border, no frame, no paper edge, no vignette: the image fills the whole frame edge to edge. A clean modern digital photograph: no creases, no fold lines, no aged-paper texture, no scratches, no film grain.
